issues.description: The Stata master repeats placeholder global-dir values and the SAS sources retain author-specific library/home roots. The effective working directories, input roots, and writable output locations are not configured for this environment.

The registered ffind helper is substantive code and declares a numeric input varlist. The master converts sic to string immediately before calling it, and its path requests ffind.ado while the registered filename is ffind.ado.ado.

The Stata master assumes an initial firm-time panel and several named prepared inputs, but no supplied Stata load step or producer is shown for them. The three SP1500 first/second/third membership-period files are distinct required inputs, and their producers and period coverage are not supplied. SAS Step 1 writes loc1.ccm3_june and loc2.ccm4; the master does not consume those names. The catalogued Compustat annual candidate exposes sich while the Stata helper call is supplied a sic variable; no mapping or panel handoff is established.

Separate from the confirmed current in-memory namespace defect in issue_bls_namespace, the supplied source does not establish the valid firm-time panel reload, NAICS/portmonth mapping, effective $dir root, or saved-file path. It also independently consumes author-prepared five- and four-digit visibility panels for the later merge and IV stage; no producer or cross-branch ratio-name mapping for those panels is supplied. Preserve these handoff and file-contract uncertainties without guessing a reload, key conversion, or aggregation.

A supported preparation step is to export/convert/copy SAS Step 6.1's mine.suecars dataset from its configured SAS home library to the Stata master's expected relative earnings surprise/suecars/suecars.dta path before Step 6.2. The source and consumer names/path are documented; no conversion was performed here. The remaining post-conversion schema, row, and history checks are tracked separately as issue_suecars_schema_history; effective roots remain under issue_paths.

After the supported SAS-to-Stata conversion/copy, the DTA storage types, row preservation/cardinality, and period/history coverage matching the separate Quarterly Controls file remain unverified. The source artifacts name the producer output fields and Stata consumer merge keys, but no converted DTA metadata or row/history check was performed; verify these contracts after conversion and before Step 6.2.

The SAS event-study block has a ticker-list input whose surrounding connection/preparation statement was withheld after credential screening. The packaged Identifier.xlsx probe exposes a gvkey header, which does not establish the ticker list or a safe construction/mapping rule.

Independently of the confirmed namespace failure in issue_dispersion_namespace, the branch does not establish a producer or intended annual-period rule for pyear. The prepared EPS, CUSIP-link, and stockprice schemas, source periods, and fiscal-period mapping remain unverified. Do not infer calendar year, portfolio year, or another grouping from yr or from a different branch.

The SAS workflow requires a remote WRDS session and sample macros. The credential/connection scan identified candidate lines in the author sources; complete surrounding blocks were withheld from display, and no credentials or connection were used. SAS/WRDS access and the exact hidden connection configuration remain unresolved.

In the supplied Master File.do, collapse by NAICS/month leaves only NAICS, month, BLSratio, and BLSratio1 in memory. The source saves that table, resets $dir, then sorts and merges on naics6d/portmonth without a use/reload between those statements. This is a confirmed current source-level namespace defect, supported by the saved source view and documented Stata collapse semantics. The intended firm-time reload and mapping are not supplied; do not invent them or treat the unresolved repair as a verified result.

The supplied Step 7.3 source collapses to disp2_2year_ahead, yr, and permno, then issues drop i n before creating i or n in the collapsed table; it also groups by pyear without a producer. This is a confirmed current source-level namespace defect in the rank branch, separate from uncertainty about a scientifically valid grouping or repair. No execution or output is inferred.

evidence.description: The documentation says output-price inflexibility data were shared by an outside researcher.
evidence.quote:
a) Output-price inflexibility

This is a proprietary dataset shared by Professor Michael Weber at the University of
Chicago Booth School of Business.

evidence.description: The documentation describes proprietary conference-call transcript collection and manual review; it is contextual unless a supplied program consumes it.
evidence.quote:
c) Analysts’ question about input costs

This is a proprietary dataset. Jin Xie hired research assistants to use Python to extract
sentences regarding analysts’ cost-related questions during conference calls. Research
assistants then manually read all the extracted sentences to improve the quality of
data. Conference-call transcripts were collected from Thomson Reuters StreetEvents
data feed. The data collection occurred during the spring of 2020.

evidence.description: The documentation names BEA, BLS, Compustat, CRSP, and I/B/E/S products and collection timing.
evidence.quote:
d) Other datasets

Firm-level financial data were collected from the Compustat North America. Stock
price data at daily and monthly frequencies were collected from the Center for
Research in Security Prices, LLC (CRSP). Analyst forecast data were collected from


                                            1

the I/B/E/S International Inc. The data collection occurred during the summer of
2020.

evidence.description: The authors describe a step-by-step data-construction workflow in the paper and shared code.
evidence.quote:
In both Section 3 of the paper and shared codes (see 5 below), a step-by-step
description is provided to enable researchers to generate a similar dataset for each of
the samples in both the manuscript and the online appendix.

evidence.description: The Stata master identifies itself as working-data construction code.
evidence.quote:
*******************************************************************************
						Gu and Xie (2023)
          
		  Price Rigidities and the Value of Public Information
			
     The "Master Code" is meant to build the working data for empirical analysis.

evidence.description: The master documents the SAS Step 1 panel/factor preparation stage.
evidence.quote:
***The purpose of Step 1 is to create a firm-time panel dataset based on Fama and French (1992).*** 

***Specifically, year t is from July of calender year t to June of calender year t+1.*** 

***We use the source code "Step1_sas_FFtiming" to achieve the following three goals"*** 
  
  ***1. Using Compustat data to calculate book value of equity***
  
  ***2. Using CRSP stock data for portfolio formation***
  
  ***3. Merging of CRSP and Compustat data***

evidence.description: The Stata workflow reads the BLS raw series panel, normalizes NAICS codes, and creates the disclosure intermediate.
evidence.quote:
global dir ".........."
use "$dir\Raw Data\BLS price (1926-2018).dta"
g d6=substr(series_id,4,6)
g d5=substr(series_id,4,5)
g d4=substr(series_id,4,4)
g d3=substr(series_id,4,3)
g n1=substr(d6,-1,1)
g n2=substr(d6,-2,2)
g n3=substr(d6,-3,3)
g naics=d6 
replace naics=d5 if n1=="-"&n2!="--"&n3!="---"
replace naics=d4 if n1=="-"&n2=="--"&n3!="---"
replace naics=d3 if n1=="-"&n2=="--"&n3=="---"
g yearmonth=string(year)+substr(period,-2,2)
